title: Find the integrating factor
text: Put the equation in the form $$y'+p\left(x\right) y=q(x)$$, then multiply by the integrating factor so the left side becomes the derivative of the integrating factor times $$y$$.

title: Integrate and solve
text: In standard form $$y'-2y=x e^x$$, and the integrating factor is $$e^{\left(-2x\right)}$$. Then the derivative of $$e^{\left(-2x\right)} y$$ is $$x e^{\left(-x\right)}$$, so $$e^{\left(-2x\right)} y=-x e^{\left(-x\right)}-e^{\left(-x\right)}+C$$. $$y(0)=-1$$ gives $$C=0$$, so $$y=-\left(x+1\right) e^x$$.
